name: Euro-area economy
summary: Euro-area GDP grew 0.4% in Q3 and the October composite PMI was 51.9; November flash PMIs not yet out
state: Eurostat estimated euro-area GDP growth of 0.4% in the third quarter, a figure confirmed in its second estimate of 13 Nov (Eurostat; RTTNews). The HCOB flash composite PMI fell to a four-month low of 51.9 in October from September, below forecasts but still above 50 (FXStreet, 23 Oct). November flash PMIs had not been published as of 20 Nov, so the latest data remain consistent with Normal.
for_you: The euro-area economy is still growing modestly. Households and firms in the region face higher borrowing costs as markets expect further ECB rate rises.
rubric_hit: Positive GDP (+0.4% Q3) and composite PMI 51.9 > 50 meet Normal

sources.title: Eurostat — GDP up by 0.4% in the euro area and by 0.5% in the EU
RTTNews — Eurozone GDP growth confirmed at 0.4%
FXStreet — Eurozone HCOB Composite PMI declines to 51.9 in October vs 52.7 expected

why: The euro area is the UK's largest trading partner; stagnation there hits UK exports and European markets.
drivers: Energy prices, German industry, ECB policy, fiscal rules, China demand.

rubric.alert: Technical recession, or PMI < 45, or bond-spread fragmentation forcing ECB action.
rubric.normal: Positive GDP growth and composite PMI > 50.
